title: Oklahoma State falls to Tulsa again despite new coach and preseason buzz
content:
Oklahoma State lost to Tulsa last season and fired coach Mike Gundy four days later in the middle of his 21st season in Stillwater.

Saturday, in its new coach’s debut, Oklahoma State fell to the in-state Golden Hurricane again, extending the longest current losing streak in the FBS to 12.

This time, Tulsa knocked off visiting Oklahoma State 24-10 in the season opener for both teams. Tulsa, a member of The American, hadn’t beaten Oklahoma State in consecutive games since 1951-52.

Oklahoma State coach Eric Morris told OSU’s radio network at halftime his team — which featured an NCAA-record 92 new players — played “as bad as you can play,” he said.

Tulsa, which entered the game as 13.5-point underdogs, won despite converting just one third down on 11 attempts. It forced four Oklahoma State turnovers and committed just one.

“I expected to win the game,” Tulsa coach Tre Lamb said, adding he didn’t like a lot of the mistakes his team made and the final score could have been 30-10 or 37-10.

Morris came to OSU from North Texas after winning 11 games a season ago. He brought quarterback Drew Mestemaker with him, fighting off a host of suitors to keep the former walk-on who never started a game in high school as the linchpin of his new program. Mestemaker signed a reported two-year deal that averages just under $4 million annually, making him one of the sport’s highest-paid quarterbacks.

Mestemaker struggled behind an offensive line that often left him scrambling. He finished 29-of-49 for 241 yards, a touchdown and two interceptions, the second coming on his final throw of the day.

Last season, he threw multiple touchdown passes in all but three games.

Oklahoma State hosts No. 2 Oregon next week and opens Big 12 play on Sept. 26 at West Virginia, where it will try to end an 18-game losing streak in Big 12 play.

Lamb, Tulsa’s second-year coach, called last year’s victory a “statement win,” adding that Tulsa was tired of being little brother to the Cowboys, whose campus is just an hour away.

The Hurricane finished 4-8 in Lamb’s first season and made headlines this offseason when the coaching staff spent two weeks living in the “Portal House,” a rental that served as the headquarters for the Golden Hurricane’s transfer portal activity.

It didn’t get as much attention as Oklahoma State’s complete roster overhaul, but Saturday, Lamb’s team saw the fruit of their efforts.

“We’re Tulsa’s team,” he said. “I’ve been saying that since I got here.”
